male.name: The Aland tur-dal farmer
male.tagline: A rainfed Lingayat farmer whose year rides on tur-dal and cotton prices.

dayInLife.text: Feeds the pair of bullocks, then walks his plot checking tur dal for pod borer damage.
Sells tur at the Kalaburagi APMC yard, sometimes waiting days for a fair price.
Cotton is picked by hand over several weeks, with his wife and mother helping.
Farm income all but stops for two to three months; he has taken hired labour nearby.
Once travelled to Hyderabad for a season of construction work after a poor monsoon.

topics.label: Daily Life & Work
topics.headline: Price swings decide whether the year is a good one
points: Sells tur through the Kalaburagi APMC, paying commission to a trader who also lends informally between harvests.
Lean period of two to three months between tur and cotton seasons, when farm income all but stops.
Draws groundwater with a diesel pump-set from a shared borewell; there is no canal command in his part of Aland.

stat.label: Tur price per quintal, Kalaburagi, 2016-17 glut

topics.label: Family & Household
topics.headline: Three generations in a two-room tiled house
points: His wife runs the home, kitchen garden and poultry, and joins the fields in cotton-picking and harvest weeks.
His mother helps with childcare and light tasks, and receives a state old-age pension.
He wants his daughter to finish SSLC (class 10) before any marriage talk; dowry expectations weigh on him.

topics.label: Education & Schooling
topics.headline: Schooling slips when harvest, buses and cost collide
points: He left school around class 8; his elder son finished class 10 but skipped PUC over commute and cotton season.
His daughter's secondary school is several kilometres away, reached by a KKRTC bus that does not always match school hours.
He hopes Article 371(J) domicile quotas might help his younger son reach a polytechnic or government job.

stat.label: Professional-course seats reserved in the region under Article 371(J) (2012)

topics.label: Health & Wellbeing
topics.headline: Long distances to care and an unrelieved farm toll
points: The family uses the taluk PHC and a private clinic; Kalaburagi's tertiary care is over an hour away.
Registered under Ayushman Bharat-Arogya Karnataka, but use is uneven and depends on which private hospitals honour it.
His wife has recurring skin irritation from cotton-picking and spraying; he has chronic back pain and mild hypertension.

topics.label: Community & Belief
topics.headline: Basavanna's legacy, a village mutt and Muslim neighbours
points: Attends the village Lingayat mutt's annual jatre; the mutt also serves as an informal dispute-resolution centre.
Has friendly ties with Muslim neighbours and has attended the Khwaja Bande Nawaz Dargah urs at least once.
Proud of Sharana and Sufi heritage, yet feels the region is labelled statistically backward without matching improvement.

topics.label: Civic Life & Government
topics.headline: Welfare reaches him; regional development promises lag
points: Deals with the gram panchayat for his MGNREGA card, land records and his mother's pension paperwork.
Gets Anna Bhagya grain and gas refills and Gruha Jyothi relief; his wife and daughter ride Shakti buses free.
Finds KKRDB-funded projects announced for his taluk slow to materialise.

stat.label: Works sanctioned 2013-14 to 2021-22; thousands not begun (CAG 2022)

topics.label: Worldview & Concerns
topics.headline: Dropout as a structural squeeze, not family neglect
points: Sees dropout as an economy forcing a choice between a classroom seat and household survival after a bad harvest.
Would demand reliable minimum support price for tur dal and cotton, and faster drought and crop-loss compensation.
Wants the promised Kalaburagi AIIMS operational, plus better rural roads and predictable KKRTC bus schedules.

schoolPressures.label: Cotton season
schoolPressures.detail: His elder son missed what would have been his first PUC year because he was needed for cotton-picking.

schoolPressures.label: Costly commutes
schoolPressures.detail: The nearest PUC with a science stream needs a daily bus commute the family judged too costly.

schoolPressures.label: Bad monsoon
schoolPressures.detail: A poor monsoon can turn into hired labour or short migration for the whole family.

schoolPressures.label: Girls' care work
schoolPressures.detail: His daughter helps with cooking and sibling care after school, which can make girls fall behind.

female.name: The Sandur Lambani woman
female.tagline: A Lambani embroiderer stitching piecework and farm wages to hold a mining household together.

dayInLife.text: Fetches water, cooks, and gets the two younger children ready for school.
Weeds or harvests on a nearby farm, taking whatever wage work is available that day.
Stitches Lambani embroidery by hand for a buyer linked to Sandur Kushala Kala Kendra.
Registers for MGNREGA work through the gram panchayat when farm and embroidery orders run out.
Carries finished pieces to Sandur or Ballari town, riding the free Shakti bus instead of an auto.

topics.label: Daily Life & Work
topics.headline: Piecework, farm wages and a husband's irregular pay
points: Embroidery is paid by the piece and depends on intermediaries reaching her hamlet, so income is unpredictable.
Her husband works at a stone-crushing and ore-loading unit near Sandur; wages depend on which units are operating.
No fixed monthly income; expenses are managed week to week, and one bad stretch strains food and school costs.

stat.label: Year Sandur Lambani embroidery received Geographical Indication status

topics.label: Family & Household
topics.headline: A double burden, and a budget she manages
points: Lives close to her husband's parents, who help with childcare and share meals with the family.
Married in her late teens; she wants her daughters to finish secondary school first.
Does most cooking, cleaning, water-fetching and childcare, and manages the day-to-day budget and her embroidery cash.

topics.label: Education & Schooling
topics.headline: Cost and distance pushed her son out after class 8
points: She never finished primary school and relies on her husband or elder daughter to read official letters and forms.
Two younger children attend a nearby government school; she is unsure a KGBV seat will open for her younger daughter.
Gor Boli at home, Kannada at school: her younger daughter needed an extra year to follow lessons comfortably.

topics.label: Health & Wellbeing
topics.headline: A husband's cough and thin access to specialist care
points: Her husband has had a persistent cough for over a year, never diagnosed at a specialist facility.
She had anaemia in later pregnancies; an ASHA worker tracked her pregnancies and her children's immunisation.
Registered under Ayushman Bharat-Arogya Karnataka but finds hospital coverage uneven; the 108 ambulance is her emergency option.

topics.label: Community & Belief
topics.headline: A close-knit tanda and an inherited craft
points: Extended family and neighbours in the tanda give help during illness, shared childcare and informal lending.
Embroidery, passed down from her mother and grandmother, is both livelihood and a marker of community identity.
Practises folk Hindu worship of tanda deities; Lambani women also keep folk songs and oral storytelling alive.

topics.label: Civic Life & Government
topics.headline: State guarantees arrive; roads and water lag behind
points: Deals with the gram panchayat for MGNREGA job card, ration card and school enrolment, and the ASHA worker for health.
Benefits from Gruha Lakshmi, Anna Bhagya, Gruha Jyothi and free Shakti bus travel.
Judges local representatives by whether promised roads, water connections and school facilities reach the tanda.

topics.label: Worldview & Concerns
topics.headline: Dropout as poverty and distance, not indifference
points: Says a child's small daily wage can matter more than a classroom seat when the household is short of cash.
Wants occupational health screening and safety enforcement at crushing units, not an end to mining jobs.
Wants fair pricing and steady market linkages so embroidery becomes a dependable livelihood, not a supplement.

schoolPressures.label: Secondary costs
schoolPressures.detail: Transport, uniforms and notebooks outweighed her son's potential wage once school was outside the tanda.

schoolPressures.label: Daily wages
schoolPressures.detail: Even small daily wages can outweigh a classroom seat when the household is short of cash.

schoolPressures.label: Monsoon roads
schoolPressures.detail: Poor road connectivity to some tandas makes attendance harder in the monsoon months.

schoolPressures.label: Language gap
schoolPressures.detail: Gor Boli at home, Kannada at school; her younger daughter needed an extra year to adjust.
